chapter_title: Chương 65: Trai Đẹp Nhất Mọi Diễn Đàn

segments.title: Chương 65: Trai Đẹp Nhất Mọi Diễn Đàn
segments.content:
Chen Jiayong, who got a free pass to Peking University for his New Concept Composition, gave up his guaranteed spot in their graduate program last year to become a reporter for the Morning News in Shanghai.

He voluntarily came to help out this year, and last night, he made half the calls to inform the contestants about meeting the admissions teachers.

At the same time, he was representing the Morning News, covering the entire New Concept Competition.

He drank at the banquet and was dizzily taking a cab back to his rented apartment.

Halfway there, his phone rang.

"Hello, hi..." Chen Jiayong answered with his eyes squinted, half-lying on the back seat of the taxi.

His university roommate's voice came through: "Old Chen, it's Qiangzi. Did you go to the New Concept event?"

Chen Jiayong sat up straight. "Just left."

"Was there a guy named Chen Guiliang who wrote two poems? And one of them was composed in seven steps?"

"Where did you hear that?"

"Just tell me if it's true."

"I guess so. How did you know? You don't follow this stuff."

"Saw it on the Peking University BBS."

After chatting with his university roommate until he got out of the car, Chen Jiayong had sobered up quite a bit. He returned to his apartment and logged into Peking University's Weiming BBS.

There were several related posts, and he casually clicked on one.

This post was quite interesting. The commenters were either classical poetry enthusiasts or top students from the Chinese Language and Literature department. They were arguing about Chen Guiliang "violating the 'lone level tone' rule."

"The third line has to be changed. Just one word and it'll be perfectly 'remedied.' Damn it, my OCD is going to act up if it's not changed."

"Yeah, it's like a fly on a cake."

"Is it possible that the author originally used 'like a sojourner's inn' but changed it to 'is a sojourner's inn' because he felt the former wasn't bold enough? Sacrificing metrical rules for artistic conception."

"I can't accept that. It would be perfect with just one word changed, why must he violate the 'lone level tone' rule? And that guy clearly did it on purpose!"

"It's definitely intentional. Otherwise, the level and oblique tones in the third and fourth lines are too much of a coincidence."

"Come on, everyone, don't be so hard on a high school student. So few people study classical poetry these days, and now that a young talent has appeared, why are you all calling for his head?"

"Big Sister, it'd be one thing if he didn't know, but this kid obviously does. He had already successfully 'remedied' it, then deliberately changed the word back. It's enough to drive someone with OCD crazy!"

"A bunch of lunatics. Has studying addled your brains? Is poetry written to adhere to metrical rules, or to express emotions and pour out one's heart? Even in Tang poetry, you can find examples of 'lone level tone' violations. Why don't you guys go and revise the entire collection of Tang poems?"

"Li Bai, Du Fu, and Gao Shi also violated the 'lone level tone' rule. Take Li Bai's 'Seeing a Guest Off in Nanyang,' for example. He only needed to change the word 'gui' (noble) to save both lines. But Li Bai didn't change it. Because he couldn't find a better word to replace it!"

"Holy crap, are you comparing a high school student to Li Bai? Don't try to ride his coattails, okay?"

"So writing poetry depends on fame and status? Does that mean only Li Bai is allowed to violate the 'lone level tone' rule? Ordinary people can't?"

"Composed in seven steps, composed in seven steps, how many times do I have to say it? Someone try taking seven steps and see what they come up with."

"..."

Chen Jiayong leaned over his computer, amused by his feuding schoolmates.

Both sides had valid points, and the argument wouldn't lead to any conclusion.

But it was indeed enough to drive someone with OCD mad. The whole poem was only four lines long, and two of them had metrical flaws. Changing just one word would fix the flaws in both lines, but Chen Guiliang stubbornly refused to change it.

Was changing "is a sojourner's inn" to "like a sojourner's inn" really that hard?

In any case, the name Chen Guiliang had become famous.

The more fiercely these people argued, the more firmly they remembered Chen Guiliang.

Chen Jiayong clicked on another post. The majority of the comments were full of astonishment and praise, with only a few snide remarks.

"Are you telling me this is an assigned essay from a high school student?"

"Even if it were written under normal circumstances, it would be a top-tier piece. But this is a competition essay with an assigned topic. From the conception and tone to the wording and prose, I can only say it's brilliant. Minor flaws in a few places can be overlooked."

"Stop the hype, it's sickening."

"Hype? You try writing one. Use the topic given in the competition. I won't even ask you to finish it in two or three hours. I'll give you two or three days and let you look up reference books. You write me a piece and let's see it!"

"Those who say it's hype probably didn't appreciate it carefully, or perhaps they didn't understand it at all. Not a single line in the entire poem is superfluous. The structure is very clean, with no sense of ostentatious piling-up of words."

"The last lines of the preface and the poem gave me goosebumps."

"The last line of the poem doesn't rhyme."

"The momentum and emotion have already built to a climax, what need is there for rhyme?"

"'I come from humble beginnings, with nothing to my name, yet I hope with this faint light to illuminate the Milky Way and all its stars.' I love this line. My parents are both laid-off workers. Although my high school days were tough, the passion in my heart has always remained. What do we poor students have besides ambition and passion? One day, we will shine with boundless radiance!"

"And 'Yet within the span of this untamed wilderness, lies the spirit to prop up heaven and earth!' The central theme of the entire poem is this sentence. Reading it made my blood boil and my scalp tingle."

"Using an object to express one's aspirations—the emphasis is on expressing aspirations. The youthful spirit in this poem is bursting forth, my computer screen can barely contain it!"

"This poem is indeed good, but it's not as miraculous as you all are making it out to be. We should view it rationally, neither elevating nor demeaning it."

"Haven't you all noticed? There are many details to dig into in this poem. The 'withered branch' held by the Black Bird is likely from the Fusang tree. I'm not just guessing, the author wrote it directly. 'Its wings brush past Fusang for thirty thousand li, its beak holds a withered stalk from the Taiyi.' Fusang is the divine Fusang tree. Taiyi is the Great Oneness, it is the Dao, the origin of heaven and earth."

"Haha, this Black Bird has quite the background."

"Carrying a branch from the tree of the universe's origin, breaking through the primordial chaos, how could this bird not have a background?"

"..."

Chen Jiayong even stopped writing his news report, just sitting there browsing the replies for fun.

Besides Peking University's Weiming BBS, posts were also being forwarded to the BBS forums of other famous universities. News traveled fast between these major institutions.

Tsinghua's Shuimu Tsinghua, Fudan's Riyue Guanghua, Shanghai Jiao Tong's Yinshui Siyuan, Zhejiang's Haina Baichuan, Wuhan's Luojia Shanshui... Alright, the names of these university BBS sites were all quite nice.

There were also some with unique styles.

For example, Xi'an Jiao Tong's Bingmayong (Terracotta Army), Nanjing's Xiaobaihe (Little Lily), Sichuan's Lanse Xingkong (Blue Starry Sky), Nankai's Wo Ai Nankai (I Love Nankai)...

In the early days of the internet, these university BBS forums were all incredibly popular, even attracting many non-student netizens to become regulars.

It was currently winter break, so there were many students and teachers idly browsing the BBS. Chen Guiliang's two poems and preface happened to become their topic of discussion.

Moreover, there were the gimmicks of "composed in seven steps" and "universities vying for him," which attracted a large number of uninformed onlookers.

Sister Furong was a regular at Shuimu Tsinghua and Weiming BBS.

She was a student at Shaanxi University of Technology, had been a class cadre, and had won scholarships. But she chose to suspend her studies to retake the college entrance exam, wanting to get into Tsinghua or Peking University.

On the eve of the exam, she was in a car accident and returned to Shaanxi University of Technology to continue her studies. After graduating, she joined a machinery factory.

Then she quit her job to prepare for the graduate school entrance exam.

She failed to get into Peking University's graduate program for two consecutive years. Her money ran out, so she found a job as an editor and continued to prepare for the exam.

Her Tsinghua and Peking University dream was shattered; she could only fulfill it on their BBS forums.

She had already started posting photos, but they weren't particularly outrageous yet, so she hadn't attracted much attention.

After work, Sister Furong returned to her rented apartment and logged into the Peking University BBS as usual.

Several hot posts caught her attention. She quickly clicked on them and read them carefully, filled with admiration for the author.

An idea struck Sister Furong. She found her favorite photo of herself and posted it with some rather unconventional remarks:

"My alluring and sexy appearance and my pure and noble temperament make me the center of attention wherever I go."

"I am the most beautiful, no one can surpass me."

"A scholar for the beauty. I feel that the author of these two poems is my perfect match. But the age gap troubles me..."

She attached the picture and clicked send.

Sister Furong kept refreshing the page, hoping to gain more attention this way.

And indeed, people replied...

"Where do you think you're going, you demon? Taste my staff!"

"It's this narcissist again."

"Is this woman nuts?"

"Go for it, OP. We support you in marching to Sichuan and confessing your love to Chen Guiliang in person!"

"Chen Guiliang: Don't you come near me, or I'll kill myself."

"OP, are you trying to make us die laughing or die of disgust?"

"..."

Sister Furong replied: "The Black Bird can carry a withered branch across the sea, so why can't I pursue my dream? I like Chen Guiliang's words, 'I hope with this faint light to illuminate the Milky Way and all its stars.' In this world, everyone has the right to shine."

"The Black Bird in this poem went through countless hardships and tribulations. I suspended my studies to retake the exam, and got into a car accident before the test. I quit my job to prepare for the grad school exam and failed twice in a row. What are these difficulties? They cannot stop me from pursuing my dream."

"I will continue to work hard and will definitely get into Peking University's graduate program next year. I'd like to quote a few lines from Chen Guiliang's poem to express my ambition: 'Though gales in the nine heavens tear at my wings, I still clutch this withered branch, refusing to yield. The stars hang inverted in a cup of water, heaven and earth overturn before my eyes. Today's men are also branch-bearing sojourners, who see monstrous waves and terrifying tides as level plains.'"

Sister Furong was very smart; she had been deliberately acting outrageous.

She had started being eccentric back when she was in the factory and had even gained some minor fame locally, occasionally getting a few commercial performance gigs.

Otherwise, how could a girl from the countryside have the funds to quit her job and prepare for the graduate school entrance exam?

She knew that speaking normally wouldn't attract attention, so her posts became more and more absurd. But today, after reading "A Journey to Yingzhou," she spoke from the heart, moved by her own feelings.

She had truly resonated with this poem.

Reading it a second time, she even felt like crying!

An article could move people, and it could also give them strength.

Sister Furong didn't look at the replies anymore. Instead, she took out a notebook and copied down the poem along with its preface.

After copying "A Journey to the Ying Sea," she refreshed the page again, and the post had new replies.

"You can do it, keep it up."

"Stop trying for Peking University's graduate program, just find a good job."

"Take my advice, Peking University's graduate program is not easy to get into."

"We'll be waiting for you by Weiming Lake."

"..."

After reading those replies, Sister Furong felt a warmth in her heart.

Reading Chen Guiliang's poem again, she felt even more motivated and decided to ramp up the absurdity in her future posts!

Compared to the immediacy of the internet, traditional media was much slower.

Chen Guiliang was already on the train, almost to Chengdu, when the first batch of reports was finally published.
